slot_note: Drawn from the author's concept note of 2026-11-11 (Concept 1, why the desk breached VaR), moved from a fully generated credit book to an equity market-making desk on the real S&P 500, Nasdaq-100 and VIX tape so the market moves and the volatility regime are published records; the desk's names, books and systems are simulated.
niche: Risk modeling (VaR/ES): a market-making desk's one-day 99% historical-simulation VaR backtest, every exception in the year traced to its cause for the supervisor's classification
analyst_test: The careful but hurried pass takes both P&Ls, replicates ERE from its methodology note on the extract each run read (matching the run log to the dollar), re-runs the 27 reused-extract nights on that day's extract and the own-history and volatility-filtered counterfactuals in the standard's order, and builds the plan's book by segment; it takes the extracts as the book held, so the two reused nights go to inputs and the four allocation nights to the model, and it prices the plan's ramp on the 30 June mapping, so the add-on rises to 0.40 instead of falling to nil.
domain_test: Replicating a historical-simulation VaR engine from its snapshot, mapping and price history, rebuilding the P&L the forecast was about from prior-close positions, and running counterfactual engines (current inputs, full own-name risk, a volatility-filtered window) to classify each exception is market-risk model validation; with another field's nouns there is no quantile forecast, no static book, no supervisor's exception classes and nothing to re-run.
layer1: a position system's schema migration with new instrument ids, a crosswalk and its cutover day in both exports
a vendor's re-sent days loaded twice and a ticker change under a stable vendor id
blotter versions: fat-finger amendments, duplicate tickets cancelled, allocations moved between client accounts
client tickets booked the next morning under their trade date
an export that repeats some lines
product control restatements mirrored by next-day ledger postings under the original value date
failed engine runs re-run on the same extract
stakeholder_role: the bank's head of market risk control, who files the quarter's exception classification with the supervisor (not named in the prompt)

spine.entity: one row is one instrument's position in one nightly extract, or one version of one ticket
spine.grain: instrument x extract (cut as the engine's run starts); ticket x version with its booking time
spine.source: synthetic, on the published S&P 500 (Cboe) and Nasdaq-100 (FRED) closes

world.org_type: broker-dealer subsidiary of a regional bank holding company

driver: The decisive quantities are the outcomes the forecast was actually about, rebuilt from the prior holdings rather than the booked totals, and each miss's survival under counterfactual forecasts that each restore one thing production lacked (the inputs it should have read, the components it left out, a scale that follows the recent spread), with the misses charged in a fixed order so the classes add back to the whole population of misses.
driver_concrete: The book the nightly forecast was about rebuilt from each extract plus the blotter's bookings made after its cut; the engine replicated from its methodology and re-run on that book, with every name on its own history and with volatility-scaled scenarios, to classify each exception under the standard's headings; the planned book priced month by month on the mapping the store rule gives for each month's first VaR.
stump: A careful solver files 16 of the 19 exceptions as the model's and the two reused-extract nights as wrong inputs, and holds an add-on that rises with the plan's ramp to USD 0.40 million, because it takes the engine's extracts as the book held and keeps the 30 June mapping through the half.
results: R1 every exception on either P&L (19: 15 booked, 18 hypothetical); R2 the 27 runs on an older extract; R3 the exceptions the inputs caused (4, all closing allocations booked after the extract; the reused extracts none); R4 risks not in the model (11); R5 the volatility heading (2), a sound model's count (2) and zone (green); R6 every exception under one heading; R7 the July add-on on the planned book (USD 0.32m); R8 the add-on August to December (0.27, 0.11, 0.08, 0.03, nil); R9 the call
one_fact_test: "ERE's position extracts are cut as each run starts, before the middle office books the day's closing-auction allocations" rescues R3, R4 and R6: 3 of 9
